YASP puts application decisions in the query path

Long image

A

Answer

YASP gives analytics clients one connection configuration while the consuming application controls query context, source-role selection, and query/result behavior.

  1. Reuse the library inside your application and bind your own callbacks.1
  2. Keep protocol handling, execution, validation, and resource limits inside the engine.2
  3. Change SQL before routing and process rows before client output.3

Applies toCurrent implementationexamples use invented names

1

What sits between the client and its source?

Diagram structure
  • Analytics client client
  • Client gateway gateway
  • Shared query engine core
  • Application callbacks callbacks
  • Schema catalog catalog
  • Backend adapter adapter
  • Selected source source
  • client → gateway · SQL
  • gateway → core · Data query
  • core → callbacks · Invoke hooks
  • gateway → catalog · Metadata
  • core → adapter · Validated route
  • adapter → source · Read-only SQL

The gateway is the client-facing connection. A backend adapter connects to the selected source and owns its credentials and native behavior.2

  1. Analytics client ↗

    Use one connection configuration. Per-query source selection does not require a client connection for every source role.

  2. Client gateway ↗

    Keep authenticated integration identity and frontend session state inside the engine.

  3. Shared query engine ↗

    Run ordered query stages and validate application decisions against configuration.

  4. Application callbacks ↗

    Supply context meanings, role mappings, SQL rules and row behavior from application code.

  5. Selected source ↗

    Execute with the configured source role. Its grants enforce source access.

2

How does a consuming application assemble it?

Diagram structure
  • Resolve settings settings
  • Bind callbacks callbacks
  • Load datasets datasets
  • Start serving listen
  • Load catalog catalog
  • Build services services
  • callbacks → datasets
  • catalog → listen
  • datasets → services
  • services → catalog
  • settings → callbacks
Application suppliesEngine supplies
Configuration, secrets and configured source identitiesValidated routes and adapter-owned credentials
Rust callbacks with bound state, or trusted Python resourcesCallback invocation, deadlines and bounded payloads
Dataset loaders and organization mappingsShared dataset publication and scoped lookup helpers
Query transformation and result rulesSQL revalidation, batch validation and client streaming

These responsibilities use the existing library and callback contracts.4

3

What happens during one ordinary query?

Diagram structure
  • Client client
  • Gateway gateway
  • App hooks app
  • Engine engine
  • Source route source
  • client → gateway · Submit SQL
  • gateway → app · Derive query context
  • app → gateway · Values + input dialect
  • gateway → app · Parsed SQL: optional modifier
  • app → gateway · Replacement or no change
  • gateway → engine · Validated effective query
  • engine → app · Choose target / login / class
  • app → engine · Application route decision
  • engine → source · Resolve bounds; execute on miss
  • source → engine · Raw columns + rows
  • engine → app · Optional bounded result batch
  • app → engine · Text / NULL edits or row filter
  • engine → gateway · Validated output chunks
  • gateway → client · Rows + emitted row count
MomentConcrete example
Client submits SQLSELECT o.id, o.total FROM logical.orders AS o
App derives contextuser_id = u17, department = finance, workload = interactive
App replaces SQLRead reporting.orders_v2 AS o while preserving the selected columns
Engine prepares executionParse replacement SQL, check read-only rules, derive its ID, and analyze optional lineage
App chooses a routetarget = reporting, backend_login = finance_reader
Source returns raw rowsSource values keep their native representation
App processes outputReplace text, set selected cells to SQL NULL, or filter rows

The original context stays available downstream. Selection uses the effective query, and result hooks receive the validated route and raw data contexts.356

4

Which capabilities are available now?

Available in the current runtimeStill planned
Bounded read-only simple-query executionPrepared statements and broader protocol/session coverage
Context, SQL modification and source-role selectionLifecycle hooks and engine interpretation of organization RBAC
Shared datasets and schema catalogAutomatic cross-dialect translation
Optional lineage, result classification and result callbacksMandatory engine-enforced dynamic masking
Opt-in raw result cachingBroader management and orchestration capabilities

Future items are outside the delivered runtime shown in the diagrams. Client protocols, backend adapters, and SQL translation have separate compatibility boundaries.72
